about: Resilio Versio demo clips. Every clip is Resilio itself, rendered offline by the project's Renderer (release sound of v2026.10.06-a6c70a4) from synthetic test signals the project generated (snare and rim one-shots, an Am-D offbeat skank at 75 bpm, a C minor pad). No recordings of other instruments or reverbs. MP3, 160 kbps, 48 kHz stereo, loudness-matched to about -20.5 LUFS integrated (EBU R128), peaks at or below -1 dBTP. Settings use panel names; knob values are 0 (fully left, 7 o'clock) to 1 (fully right, 5 o'clock), with approximate clock positions.

clips.title: Dry, then wet
clips.caption: A one-drop groove: two bars dry, then two bars through the Tubby snare splash starting point.
clips.transcript: A snare on beat three with rim clicks around it, at 75 bpm. For two bars it is dry and close. Then the reverb comes in: each snare gets a bright crack and a loose, dripping spring tail with a little tape grit, ringing out after the last hit.

clips.title: TANK 1, then TANK 2
clips.caption: One snare into one spring (sparse, the most splashy), then the same snare into two springs (the classic tank).
clips.transcript: A single snare hit, twice. First with one spring: a splashy, sparse tail where you can hear the individual boings. Then with two springs: a denser, smoother tail of the same length.
clips.note: Two renders joined back to back.

clips.title: CLEAN, TAPE, VALVE
clips.caption: The same snare through each ATTITUDE, with DRIVE at 1:30: polite, then tape-saturated, then a cranked valve stage.
clips.transcript: A single snare hit, three times. CLEAN: a clear, polite spring tail. TAPE: warmer, slightly saturated, with a fine grain. VALVE: harder and rougher, a rattle on the hit and a gritty tail.
clips.note: Three renders joined back to back.

clips.title: The throw
clips.caption: Only the snares on bars 2 and 4 go into the springs (THROW held for each); everything else stays dry, and each tail rings on.
clips.transcript: The one-drop groove, mostly dry. On the second bar's snare the springs open for that one hit, and a long tail rings on under the following bar. The same happens on the fourth bar's snare, and its tail rings out at the end.

settings.THROW / TAP: pressed once at the start (throw mode on), then held for the snares of bars 2 and 4

clips.title: SPLASH
clips.caption: SPLASH fully down for two bars, then at 4 o'clock: the same hits ring the springs much harder.
clips.transcript: The one-drop groove through the reverb. For two bars the tail is smooth and even. Then the hits clang into the springs: a brighter, harder crash on each snare and rim, while the quiet ghost notes stay quiet.

clips.title: King Tubby's Big Knob
clips.caption: TONE ridden from noon to fully right and back while the groove plays: the tail thins to a telephone splash, then the warmth returns.
clips.transcript: The one-drop groove with a long tail. TONE sweeps up: the reverb loses its low end and turns thin, bright and telephone-like, with a nasal ring on the snare. It holds there for a few seconds, then sweeps back and the body returns.

settings.TONE: 0.5 (12) to 1 (5) from 2.6 s to 7 s, held, back to 0.5 by 13.5 s

clips.title: WOBBLE: drift, then warble
clips.caption: A held pad: WOBBLE left of noon drifts like worn tape, then right of noon becomes a steady warble.
clips.transcript: A soft C minor pad chord in a mostly wet spring. For the first half the reverb's pitch drifts slowly and unevenly, like old tape. Then it changes to a regular, even vibrato until the chord fades.

clips.title: Skank into echo
clips.caption: TANK ECHO clocked at 75 bpm, TENSION on dotted 1/8: offbeat chords into a worn tape echo feeding the springs.
clips.transcript: Offbeat A minor and D chord stabs at 75 bpm. Each stab is answered by tape repeats on a dotted eighth, getting darker each time, each with a short spring halo. After the chords stop, the repeats fade out.

clips.title: VALVE Howl
clips.caption: The Drowned Howl starting point: one snare tips the tank into its own feedback; at 10 seconds DECAY comes back down and it falls away.
clips.transcript: One snare hit, then a rough, moving roar that keeps going on its own: the springs feeding back, shifting in pitch and texture, never a pure tone. After about ten seconds it falls quickly into a normal tail and fades to silence.

clips.title: The Hold
clips.caption: CLEAN with DECAY fully up: a pad blooms into a held bed that keeps ringing after the chord stops at 8 seconds.
clips.transcript: A C minor pad fades in and blooms into a wide, still wash. At eight seconds the chord itself stops, but the wash carries on, held and slowly fading, to the end of the clip.
